listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Monday, October 12, 2026. Our lead story is about Ukraine. President Trump announced a partial ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine focused on energy infrastructure. Ukraine's leader says Russia is continuing to attack and is ignoring that energy ceasefire. A BBC report says six Ukrainian energy sites have been hit since the announcement, according to President Zelensky. The reports ask whether either country knew about the deal in advance. Now the other front page stories. India's opposition parties marched to the top court as protests over voter list revisions escalate. More than 130 million names have been removed from the voter roll. Katie Zacharia, who worked for one of Trump's companies, will be the new White House press secretary. The actor RJ Mitte, who played Walter White Jr in Breaking Bad, has died aged 34. Immigration agents searched the home of Congresswoman Ilhan Omar. She called it an attempt to target political enemies. In tech and AI, Python 3.15 is now out. Researchers report blood cells from an 80-year-old donor were turned into stem cells with a molecular age under 20. In politics, nearly 22 million dollars in taxpayer funds has been spent on ads. In world news, NPR reports many Iranians who take jobs in Turkey are exploited. A Qantas flight from Italy to Australia was cancelled after reports of bug bites. In sports, Brendan Allen beat Christian Leroy Duncan by submission in the fifth round of the UFC main event. The 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw was suspended one game without pay. In Atlanta, President Trump will campaign with Congressman Mike Collins and Rick Jackson, with a rally in Dalton on Friday. Brookhaven residents asked the council to delay a fire station agreement at Blackburn Park. In architecture, a trio of modern homes in Old Fourth Ward is coming to market this month. In science, NASA says experiments on human and plant health are heading to the space station. Antarctic sea ice reached its 2026 maximum, the third lowest since satellite records began. That is the brief. Have a good day.

lead.title: Trump announced a partial Russia-Ukraine ceasefire. Did either country know about it?
lead.note: President Trump announced a partial ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine focused on energy infrastructure. Ukraine's leader says Russia is continuing to attack Ukraine and is ignoring what Trump called an energy ceasefire. The report asks whether either country knew about the announcement beforehand. A BBC report today says six Ukrainian energy sites have been hit by Russia since the ceasefire was announced, according to Zelensky. Reports say the US president stated energy infrastructure would not be targeted, yet strikes have continued. For a reader following world news, this is a clear test of whether a announced pause holds in practice. The story is still developing, and the sources so far are statements from the leaders involved.
